title: PAST PERFECT
subtitle: Simple & continuous · el pasado del pasado

map.center: El PAST PERFECT es el «pasado del pasado»: algo que ocurrió antes de otro momento pasado.

nodes.title: Continuous
items: I had been waiting for an hour.
Duración antes de un momento pasado.

nodes.title: ¿Cuándo se usa?
items: Dos acciones pasadas: la más antigua → past perfect.
When I arrived, the film had started.

nodes.title: Palabras clave
nodes.after: By the time we arrived, they had gone.

nodes.title: Simple o continuous
items: Duración: I was tired — I'd been running.

nodes.title: Consejo rápido

error.title: Error común

mini.es: Completa con el past perfect (simple o continuous).

items.q: When we arrived, the film ___ (start).
She ___ (never / fly) before that trip.
I ___ (wait) for an hour when he came.
By the time I got up, they ___ (go).
___ you ever been there before?

explain.es: El past perfect sirve para hablar de algo que pasó antes de otro momento del pasado. Es el «pasado del pasado», como el pluscuamperfecto español (había comido, había salido). Es imprescindible para contar historias: cuando ya estamos en un momento pasado y queremos mirar todavía más atrás, como en un flashback de una película. Tiene dos formas: simple (had done) y continuous (had been doing).
explain.en: The past perfect describes something that happened <mark>before another past moment</mark>: the past of the past.

explain.title: 1 · Past perfect simple
explain.es: Se forma con had + participio (la 3.ª columna de los irregulares) y es igual para todas las personas: no hay has ni terminaciones. En la conversación se contrae: I'd, you'd, she'd, they'd… En español cambia el auxiliar (había, habías, habíamos); en inglés, siempre had.
explain.en: had + past participle, the same for all persons. Short form: 'd.
formula: I / you / he / she / we / they + *had* + participio

examples.en: When I got to the station, the train had already left.
examples.es: Cuando llegué a la estación, el tren ya se había ido.

examples.en: She had worked in Paris before she moved to Madrid.
examples.es: Había trabajado en París antes de mudarse a Madrid.

examples.en: We'd never seen such a beautiful beach until we went to Menorca.
examples.es: Nunca habíamos visto una playa tan bonita hasta que fuimos a Menorca.

explain.title: 2 · Negativa y preguntas
explain.es: Negativa: hadn't (had not) + participio. Pregunta: Had + sujeto + participio…? Respuestas cortas: Yes, I had. / No, I hadn't. Con palabras interrogativas: Where had you put it? ¡Sin did!
explain.en: Negative: hadn't + participle. Question: Had + subject + participle…? No did.

examples.en: I hadn't finished my presentation when the meeting started.
examples.es: No había terminado la presentación cuando empezó la reunión.

examples.en: Had you ever been abroad before that trip? — No, I hadn't.
examples.es: ¿Habías estado alguna vez en el extranjero antes de ese viaje? — No.
¿Por qué se había ido tan pronto?

explain.title: 3 · Past perfect continuous
explain.es: Se forma con had been + -ing. Lo usamos para una actividad que estuvo ocurriendo durante un tiempo hasta un momento del pasado (o justo antes). Responde a How long…? y suele ir con for / since. También explica efectos visibles en el pasado. Truco: el español llevaba + tiempo + gerundio = had been + -ing + for.
explain.en: had been + -ing: an activity in progress for some time up to a past moment, often with for / since, or explaining a visible past result.

examples.en: I had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally arrived.
examples.es: Llevaba una hora esperando cuando por fin llegó el autobús.

examples.en: Her eyes were red because she had been crying.
examples.es: Tenía los ojos rojos porque había estado llorando.

examples.en: They had been living in Bristol for ten years when they decided to move.
examples.es: Llevaban diez años viviendo en Bristol cuando decidieron mudarse.

explain.title: Todo junto: simple y continuous
head: Forma · Form
✅ Afirmativa
⛔ Negativa
❓ Pregunta
💬 Respuesta corta
rows: Yes, I had. / No, I hadn't.
Yes, he had. / No, he hadn't.
Yes, they had. / No, they hadn't.
explain.note: Ojo: 'd puede ser had o would. Si detrás va un participio (she'd gone) o been (she'd been working) → had. Si va un infinitivo (she'd go) → would.

explain.title: 4 · Contar historias: el orden de los hechos
explain.es: En una narración, el past simple cuenta la historia principal (lo que va pasando) y el past perfect nos hace saltar hacia atrás para explicar lo que había ocurrido antes. Una vez que el lector sabe que estamos «más atrás», podemos volver al past simple.
explain.en: Past simple = the main story line. Past perfect = a flashback to an earlier event.

examples.en: When I opened the door, I realised someone had broken into the flat.
examples.es: Cuando abrí la puerta, me di cuenta de que alguien había entrado a robar en el piso.

examples.en: The party was a disaster: the DJ hadn't turned up and the food had run out.
examples.es: La fiesta fue un desastre: el DJ no había aparecido y se había acabado la comida.

examples.en: She recognised him at once. They had met at a conference years before.
examples.es: Lo reconoció enseguida. Se habían conocido en un congreso años antes.

explain.title: ¿Past simple o past perfect?
explain.es: Con when, el tiempo verbal cambia el significado: past simple + past simple = una cosa justo después de la otra; past perfect = una cosa ya había pasado antes.
explain.en: With when, the tense changes the meaning.

cols.head: ▶️ Past simple · una tras otra
items: When the police came, the thief ran away.
Llegó la policía y el ladrón huyó.

cols.head: ⏮️ Past perfect · ya había pasado
items: When I arrived, the film had started.
Cuando llegué, la peli ya había empezado.
When the police came, the thief had run away.
Cuando llegó la policía, el ladrón ya había huido.

explain.title: 5 · Palabras clave
head: Expresión
Ejemplo · Example
rows: By the time we got there, the shop had closed.
After she had finished her degree, she travelled.
When I woke up, everyone had gone out.
As soon as he had paid, he left.
I didn't relax until I had sent the email.
explain.note: By the time + past simple → la otra parte casi siempre va en past perfect: By the time I arrived, they had eaten.
explain.note_en: By the time + past simple → past perfect in the main clause.

explain.title: 6 · already, just, never, ever, yet
explain.es: Las mismas palabras que usas con el present perfect funcionan con el past perfect, pero mirando a un momento pasado. Van entre had y el participio: had already left, had just arrived, had never tried. Ever se usa en preguntas. Yet va al final en negativas y preguntas: They hadn't arrived yet. Y el español acababa de + infinitivo = had just + participio.
explain.en: already, just, never and ever go between had and the participle. yet goes at the end.

examples.en: The guests had already arrived when I got home.
examples.es: Los invitados ya habían llegado cuando llegué a casa.

examples.en: I'd just sat down when the phone rang.
examples.es: Me acababa de sentar cuando sonó el teléfono.

examples.en: Had you ever tried sushi before you went to Japan?
examples.es: ¿Habías probado alguna vez el sushi antes de ir a Japón?

explain.title: ¿Simple o continuous?
explain.es: Usa el simple para una acción terminada o un resultado / cantidad (¿cuánto?, ¿cuántos?). Usa el continuous para la duración de una actividad (¿cuánto tiempo?) o para explicar algo que se notaba después. Los verbos de estado (know, like, believe, own) no van en continuous.
explain.en: Simple = finished action / how many. Continuous = duration / how long, or visible effects. State verbs → simple.

cols.head: ⏳ Continuous · duración
items: He was wet: he had been swimming.

explain.title: 7 · ¿Cuándo NO hace falta?
explain.es: Si el orden de los hechos ya está claro con before o after, o si contamos las acciones en el orden en que pasaron, el past simple es suficiente. El past perfect no es «más correcto»: solo hace falta cuando hay que retroceder en el tiempo. ¡No lo uses por todo!
explain.en: If the order is already clear (before / after, or events told in sequence), the past simple is enough.

examples.en: I had breakfast, got dressed and left for work.
examples.es: Desayuné, me vestí y me fui a trabajar.

examples.en: After she finished / had finished the exam, she went home.
examples.es: Después de terminar el examen, se fue a casa. (las dos valen)
Nos fuimos antes de que acabara el concierto.

items.en: By the time the firefighters arrived, the fire had spread to the roof.
items.es: Para cuando llegaron los bomberos, el fuego se había extendido al tejado.

items.en: I was nervous because I had never spoken in public before.
items.es: Estaba nervioso porque nunca había hablado en público.

items.en: She had been studying for six hours, so she took a break.

items.en: When I checked my account, I saw that my salary hadn't arrived.

items.en: He realised he had left his passport at the hotel.
items.es: Se dio cuenta de que se había dejado el pasaporte en el hotel.

items.en: We had been driving for hours when we finally found a petrol station.
items.es: Llevábamos horas conduciendo cuando por fin encontramos una gasolinera.

items.en: Had you met Laura before the wedding?
items.es: ¿Ya conocías a Laura antes de la boda?

items.en: It was the first time I had seen the sea.
items.es: Era la primera vez que veía el mar.

items.en: My feet hurt because I had been walking all day.
items.es: Me dolían los pies porque había estado andando todo el día.

items.en: The company had lost a lot of money, so it closed two shops.
items.es: La empresa había perdido mucho dinero, así que cerró dos tiendas.

items.en: I didn't recognise her: she had changed so much!
They had just got married when they moved to Canada.
items.es: Se acababan de casar cuando se mudaron a Canadá.

items.bad: When I arrived, the train already left.
items.good: When I arrived, the train had already left.

items.bad: I had been knowing him for years.
items.why: know es de estado: no va en continuous.

items.bad: I was waiting for two hours when he arrived.
items.good: I had been waiting for two hours when he arrived.
items.why_en: Duration up to a past moment.

items.bad: It was the first time I saw snow.
items.good: It was the first time I had seen snow.
items.why: It was the first time → past perfect (español: veía).
items.why_en: It was the first time + past perfect.

items.bad: By the time we arrived, they left.
items.good: By the time we arrived, they had left.
items.why: By the time + past simple → past perfect.

items.bad: Did you had eaten before the class?
items.why: La pregunta se hace con had, sin did.
items.why_en: No did in past perfect questions.

items.bad: I had breakfast, had got dressed and had left.
items.why: Acciones en orden → past simple. ¡No abuses!

items.es: Busca el momento de referencia en el pasado: when I arrived, by 2010, at 9 pm…
¿Esta acción ocurrió antes de ese momento? → past perfect. ¿Al mismo tiempo o después? → past simple.
items.en: Earlier → past perfect; same time or later → past simple.

items.es: ¿Importa la duración (how long, for, since) o se ve el efecto? → had been + -ing. ¿Resultado o cantidad? → had + participio.
¿El orden ya está claro (before, after, una acción tras otra)? Puedes usar el past simple.
items.en: Order already clear → past simple is fine.

items.es: Revisa: had para todas las personas, participio correcto (gone, seen, written) y adverbio entre had y el participio.
items.en: Check: had for all persons, participle, adverb position.

lines.en: What a day! When I got to the airport, my flight had been cancelled.
lines.es: ¡Menudo día! Cuando llegué al aeropuerto, me habían cancelado el vuelo.

lines.en: Oh no! Hadn't they sent you an email?
lines.es: ¡Oh, no! ¿No te habían mandado un email?

lines.es: Sí, pero yo no había mirado el correo desde por la mañana.

lines.en: So how long did you have to wait?
I'd been waiting for four hours when they finally found me a seat on another flight.
lines.es: Llevaba cuatro horas esperando cuando por fin me encontraron sitio en otro vuelo.

lines.en: And by the time you landed, the meeting had finished, right?
lines.es: Y para cuando aterrizaste, la reunión ya había terminado, ¿no?

lines.en: Exactly. Everyone had already gone home. I'd never felt so frustrated!
lines.es: Exacto. Todos se habían ido ya a casa. ¡Nunca me había sentido tan frustrada!

explain.title: Truco: la línea del tiempo
explain.es: Dibuja una línea del tiempo con dos marcas en el pasado: 1 = lo más antiguo, 2 = lo más reciente. La marca 1 lleva had. Y recuerda los «amigos» del español: había + participio = had + participio; llevaba + tiempo + gerundio = had been + -ing for; acababa de = had just.
explain.en: Draw a timeline: the earlier event gets had.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee la historia. Marca T (true) o F (false) y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the story. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Last September, Daniel started a new job at a bank in London. He had prepared everything the night before: he had ironed his shirt, packed his bag and set two alarms. He had never been so nervous.

But the next morning, things went wrong. There had been a power cut during the night, so his alarms hadn't gone off. When he finally woke up, it was already half past eight. By the time he reached the station, his train had left.

He arrived at the office forty minutes late. He had been running for ten minutes and his face was bright red. His new boss, Mrs Clarke, smiled and said: “Don't worry. On my first day, I got on the wrong train and ended up in Brighton!” Daniel laughed. It was the first time he had relaxed all morning.

items.q: Daniel had prepared his things the night before.
His alarms didn't go off because his phone was broken.
items.why: There had been a power cut during the night.

items.q: He caught his usual train.
items.why: By the time he reached the station, his train had left.

items.q: His boss was angry with him.
items.why: She smiled and told him not to worry.

items.q: What had Daniel done the night before?
items.a: He had ironed his shirt, packed his bag and set two alarms.

items.q: Why was his face red when he arrived?
items.a: Because he had been running for ten minutes.

items.q: Find a past perfect continuous in the text.
items.a: He had been running (for ten minutes).

items.q: What happened to Mrs Clarke on her first day?
items.a: She got on the wrong train and ended up in Brighton.

items.a: Ej.: I was exhausted last Friday because I had been working on a project all week.

items.a: Ej.: When Clara opened the door, she knew something was wrong. Someone had been in the flat. The window was open and her laptop had disappeared.

checklist.es: Formo el past perfect simple: had + participio (igual para todos).
checklist.en: I can form the past perfect simple.

checklist.es: Formo el past perfect continuous: had been + -ing.
checklist.en: I can form the past perfect continuous.

checklist.es: Sé cuándo algo pasó antes de otro momento pasado.
checklist.en: I can show that something happened earlier in the past.

checklist.es: Uso by the time, already, just, never… before.
checklist.en: I can use by the time, already, just, never… before.
I can choose between simple and continuous.

checklist.es: No abuso del past perfect: si el orden está claro, uso el past simple.
checklist.en: I don't overuse the past perfect.
